summary: Mark Tatz was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz in 1978, studied with several traditional teachers, and was attested as a professor at CIIS in 1988.

Mark Teeuwen specializes in Japanology and religious studies. He completed his MA and PhD at Leiden University, lectured at Cardiff University from 1994 to 1999, and became a professor at the University of Oslo in 1999.
Mark Wilks was a historian and Indologist. He served as Resident in the Kingdom of Mysore (~1803–1808) and Governor of Saint Helena (~1813–1816), and became a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1826.
Mark William Carr worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as Assistant Inspector General in the Madras Police in 1862 and became a Major in the Madras Staff Corps in 1870.
Mark Zebrowski was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Dartmouth College (~1962–1966) and Harvard University.

Markus Gabriel is a philosopher who studied at the University of Bonn. He has held professorships and directorships at Bonn since 2009, previously taught at Heidelberg and The New School, and took appointments at Kyoto University and the Kyoto Institute of Philosophy.

Markus Viehbeck works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna in 2012 under Helmut Tauscher and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, later working as a project researcher at Heidelberg and faculty at Vienna (attested 2026).

Marsha Weidner is a scholar of Sinology, art history, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley, and held posts at the University of Virginia (attested 1990) and the University of Kansas (attested 2001).

Marshall Livingston Perrin was a linguist who studied at Harvard and earned his PhD at Göttingen. He taught at Göttingen (1885–1888) and Boston University, where he became Assistant Professor in 1888 and Professor of Sanskrit in 1910.

Marshall Sahlins was a historian and anthropologist who studied at the University of Michigan and Columbia University. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1957–1973) and the University of Chicago from 1973.
Marta Bianco specializes in Sinology and Tibetology. She completed two master's degrees at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (in 2023 and 2025), where she became a PhD candidate in 2024.

Marta Sanvido is a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at Ca' Foscari University, UC Berkeley, and the University of Hamburg, before becoming an Assistant Professor at Yale University in 2025.

Marta Sernesi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She received her PhD from the University of Turin in 2007 and served as a visiting professor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Martha A. Muusses was an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who completed her PhD at Utrecht under Willem Caland. She worked at the Batavian Society of Arts and Sciences and taught Dutch at Copenhagen, Stockholm, Uppsala, and Gothenburg.

Martha Ann Selby is an Indologist who is Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin and serves as Sangam Professor of South Asian Studies and Department Chair at Harvard University (attested 2026).
Martha Lile Love was an Indologist. She earned a B.A. from the University of Toronto and pursued further studies at Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martha Nussbaum is a philosopher who studied at NYU and Harvard, and under Bernard Williams. She taught at Harvard and Brown before becoming Ernst Freund Distinguished Service Professor of Law and Ethics at the University of Chicago in 1995.

Martin Baumann is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at Leibniz University Hannover and his Habilitation at Leipzig, becoming Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Lucerne in 2001.

Martin Brauen is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at Zurich and Delhi under several traditional teachers. He held curatorial and leadership roles at the Ethnographic Museum of the University of Zurich and the Rubin Museum.

Martin Collcutt specializes in Japanology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Cambridge and Harvard (PhD 1975) and served on the faculty at Princeton University from 1975 to 2015, where he directed the East Asian Studies Program.
